claims.text: Optimizing the phosphorus-to-silicon ratio in MnFeP-Si compounds improves their magnetocaloric properties.
The phosphorus-to-silicon ratio tunes the first-order magnetic phase transition in MnFeP-Si compounds.
Changing the phosphorus-to-silicon ratio alters the lattice structure.
Compositional tuning modifies the electronic characteristics of MnFeP-Si compounds.
Compositional tuning modifies lattice strain in MnFeP-Si compounds.
The modified electronic and lattice-strain characteristics reduce hysteresis.
The modified electronic and lattice-strain characteristics enhance the magnetic entropy change.
An optimized phosphorus-to-silicon ratio produces greater refrigerant capacity than the baseline composition.
An optimized phosphorus-to-silicon ratio produces a larger magnetic entropy change than the baseline composition.
An optimized phosphorus-to-silicon ratio reduces hysteresis losses relative to the baseline composition.
The proposed enhancement occurs only within a narrow compositional window.
Compositions outside the optimal window may diminish the magnetocaloric enhancement or introduce undesired thermal hysteresis.
The degree of magnetocaloric improvement is sensitive to synthesis conditions.
The degree of magnetocaloric improvement is sensitive to precise compositional adjustments.
